rationale: Demonstrate subtraction by counting back along a number line step by step, showing clearly that each hop lands on a new number rather than counting the start number as a hop.

script.focus: Notice how the first hop moves from 14 to 13, counting the movement rather than the starting number.

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: Notice how the first hop moves from 14 to 13, counting the movement rather than the starting number.

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly addresses the exact misconception ('counts the starting number as the first hop') with clear, targeted narration explaining that standing at the start is hop 0 and hop 1 lands on 13. Being a passive demo rather than an active task makes it simpler/lower cognitive load, though it uses the same number-line representation.
judgement.verdict: Yes, a teacher would gladly use this worked demonstration to directly model that movement—not the starting number—is what gets counted.
